newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops seize northern rebel town.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops seize northern rebel town.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops captured a rebel town on Monday after resuming their offensive in the northern Wanni region controlled by Tamil Tiger rebels, military officials in the north said.
They said troops of Operation "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory" captured Puliyankulam, some 22 km (14 miles) north of the government-held town of Vavuniya.
Rebel resistance was not heavy, they added.
Troops moved out of their camps on two flanks at dawn on Monday in an attempt to converge at Puliyankulam, which was held by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels.
The troops moved from their positions in Nedunkeni and Periyamadu after consolidating these areas following an attack by the LTTE on the army's rear two weeks ago, they said.
It was the column from Periyamadu that captured Puliyankulam, military officials said.
A Defence Ministry spokesman in Colombo said only that troops were near Puliyankulam and that they had overcome resistance from the rebels.
At least eight soldiers were killed and 60 wounded when the rebels fired artillery and mortars at troops at Omanthai, south of Periyamadu, on Monday morning, the military officials said.
Police commandos lying in ambush in the same area killed seven rebels trying to infiltrate military defences, they said.

Two weeks ago, the rebels mounted a surprise attack on the military's rear near the northern government-held town of Vavuniya, some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, delaying the main offensive.

Since then no major battles have been reported in the north although the troops and the separatists were involved in low-intensity warfare as the military tried to clear areas before resuming its advance.
Some 20,000 troops launched the offensive last month through the brush jungle of the Wanni to open a crucial highway linking Vavuniya with the Jaffna peninsula, a further 100 km (60 miles) north.
Jaffna city was controlled by the rebels for nearly a decade before being captured by government forces last year.
The rebels, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east, have now set up base in the Wanni.
The clandestine rebel Voice of Tiger radio, monitored in Vavuniya, said on Monday the army had launched a heavy shelling attack in the Puliyankulam area on Sunday. It did not give details.
Independent confirmation of events is not possible as the international media have not been allowed in the war zone.

Sri Lanka President Chandrika Kumaratunga was quoted as saying by the state-run Daily News on Monday that there was a need to crush the rebels militarily before finding a political solution to the ethnic strife.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
